relationships.description: The information right names the single information category (such as payment card data) on which its grantee may perform the listed read or modify operations.
relationships.evidence: The right's declaration in the security model or policy file references the information entity's identifier as its target, alongside the list of permitted operations.

relationships.description: The information right is granted directly to this named principal, making that user population, service account or external party the sole holder of the listed operations.
relationships.evidence: The grant record or policy entry lists the actor's identifier as its grantee or subject, for example a service account name in the subject field of the access rule.

relationships.description: The access condition is one attribute comparison that must evaluate true at decision time for the information right to take effect, and it supplies the denial message when it fails.
relationships.evidence: The right's condition expression in the policy definition includes the access condition's attribute, operator and value, and the authorization engine evaluates it before granting access.

relationships.description: The information right sets the rules for who may handle the information category and which operations are permitted on it, so it acts as a usage rule for that category.
relationships.evidence: The data governance catalog or classification register lists the right as an access rule attached to the information entity, next to its sensitivity classification.

relationships.description: The information right is a principal-specific, condition-qualified instance of the abstract action-on-resource permission and enforces it directly for one actor instead of through a role.
relationships.evidence: The right's definition references the permission identifier, and its operations match that permission's action and scope, so enforcement points checking the permission also accept the right.

notes: 'governs' to InformationEntity largely duplicates 'accesses' to the same entity; both state that the right targets one information category. 'implements' Permission is questionable, because the spec defines InformationRight as distinct from a role-assigned Permission. 'realizes' or 'references' may fit better.
